name: Bunnie Huang
milestone_by_age_26: As an MIT EE PhD student, reverse-engineered the original Microsoft Xbox security system after its Nov 2001 launch and published the foundational AI Memo 'Keeping Secrets in Hardware: the Microsoft Xbox Case Study' (May 2002), the first widely cited public analysis of Xbox hardware security, at about age 26–27.
early_history_summary: Born 1975 in Kalamazoo, Michigan, to Chinese parents who had fled to Taiwan; middle of three children. Attended MIT from 1992, earned a PhD in electrical engineering in 2002, and built a reputation for silicon-level reverse engineering while still a graduate student, culminating in the Xbox security work that later became the free book Hacking the Xbox.
family_context_summary: Born in Kalamazoo to mainland Chinese parents who fled to Taiwan; father from central China, mother Beijing-born with Mongol heritage. Father bought an Apple II clone when bunnie was about seven, seeding early electronics curiosity.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not professional hardware engineers in reviewed sources; early home computer access from father is the clearest domain-adjacent support.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT EE PhD, early home computing, Xbox console security wave, reverse-engineering depth
evidence_summary: Huang's breakout was silicon-level reverse engineering of the original Xbox as an MIT graduate student, published as an AI Memo in May 2002 and later expanded into Hacking the Xbox. Elite MIT pipeline, long prior electronics reps from childhood, and scarce hardware-security skill depth are the strongest documented advantages; family wealth and networks are only lightly documented via early home computer access.
starting_point: Born 1975 in Kalamazoo, Michigan, to Chinese immigrant parents; early access to an Apple II clone and later MIT electrical engineering path.
current_position: Independent hardware hacker, author (The Hardware Hacker; Essential Guide to Electronics in Shenzhen), open-hardware designer (Novena, Precursor), and HAX advisor; long associated with Singapore/Shenzhen manufacturing ecosystems.

trajectory.event: MIT autonomous underwater vehicle team won the AUVSI competition while he was a graduate student.
Published AI Memo documenting reverse engineering of original Xbox hardware security (work begun after Nov 2001 launch).
Published Hacking the Xbox: An Introduction to Reverse Engineering (later released free after Aaron Swartz's death).
Became hardware lead at Chumby, designing open-source consumer hardware platforms.
Received EFF Pioneer Award for hardware hacking, open source, and activism.
Crowdfunded open-hardware Novena laptop beyond its $250k goal (final ~$723k).
Co-published phone introspection research with Edward Snowden and joined EFF DMCA 1201 challenge.

name: Naomi Wu
milestone_by_age_26: Designed and publicly documented the 3D-printed Wu Ying 'hacker heels' with embedded pentest tools (keylogger, wireless router, lockpicks) in 2015 at about age 21, launching her SexyCyborg persona as a widely covered Shenzhen maker; by 2018 (age 23–24) she was the first Chinese person on the cover of Make magazine.
early_history_summary: Shenzhen-based self-taught maker and Ruby on Rails programmer who built wearable and open-source hardware projects while working under a masculine coding pseudonym to avoid gender bias. Combined flamboyant public persona with technical demos to challenge stereotypes about women in Chinese hardware culture.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; she has carefully limited personal biographical disclosure for safety reasons in China.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Shenzhen Huaqiangbei ecosystem, maker platform audience, open-source hardware wave, women-in-STEM visibility
evidence_summary: Wu's ≤26 milestone is public technical maker work and platform fame from Shenzhen, especially the 2015 hacker heels and subsequent Make cover, not a VC-backed company founding. Living inside the world's densest electronics manufacturing ecosystem plus aggressive online distribution are the clearest advantages; family background is intentionally under-documented.
starting_point: Born 30 August 1994; based in Shenzhen, China; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Chinese DIY maker and open-source advocate (SexyCyborg); activity reduced since mid-2023 after reported police pressure over security commentary; named maintainer of The Essential Guide to Electronics in Shenzhen (2023).

trajectory.event: Published Wu Ying 3D-printed hacker heels with embedded pentest tools, drawing international maker press.
Public dispute with Make CEO Dale Dougherty over authenticity; Dougherty apologized; listed among influential women in 3D printing.
First Chinese person on the cover of Make magazine; Sino:Bit open-source educational board certified by OSHWA.
Detained after Wall Street Journal / Patriot Act interview segment on Chinese censorship.
Became maintainer of Essential Guide to Electronics in Shenzhen; public social activity sharply reduced after security-app criticism.

name: Adam Savage
category: Special effects designer / TV science communicator
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable breakout by age 26 (1993). MythBusters premiered in 2003 at age 35–36; major film model/special-effects credits (Galaxy Quest, Star Wars Episode II, The Matrix Reloaded, etc.) cluster in the late 1990s–early 2000s well after 26. Early child acting and craft work are not treated as the career-defining milestone.
family_context_summary: Born New York City; raised in Sleepy Hollow, NY. Father Whitney Lee Savage was a painter/animator (Sesame Street, Electric Company); mother Karen a psychotherapist.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional animator and filmmaker, providing artistic/making culture proximity.
evidence_summary: Fame and defining career milestone arrived with MythBusters (2003) in his mid-30s after years of film special-effects work. No specific dated material founder/operator or research breakout by age 26 found in reviewed sources.

name: Jamie Hyneman
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 (1982). MythBusters co-hosting began in 2003 at age 46–47; professional special-effects career and M5 Industries ownership are documented from the mid-1980s onward (years active listed from 1985, age ~29), after the age-26 cutoff.
family_context_summary: Born Marshall, Michigan; early life includes running away at 14 and varied jobs (boat captain, pet shop, animal wrangler) before special effects.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a special-effects family pipeline in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Defining public success was MythBusters starting 2003 at age ~47; earlier SFX entrepreneurship and M5 Industries postdate age 26. No dated material breakout by 26 found.

name: Ankit Bhati
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Ola Cabs (ANI Technologies) with Bhavish Aggarwal in December 2010 / early 2011 at about age 23, serving as technical cofounder/CTO of what became one of India's largest ride-hailing platforms.
early_history_summary: IIT Bombay mechanical engineering undergrad who continued into M.Tech (CAD & automation), finishing around 2010. Built freelance websites in college, then partnered with classmate Bhavish Aggarwal to launch a cab aggregation service after an early trip-planning experiment, with Bhati owning the technology stack.
family_context_summary: Sources place origins in Jodhpur, Rajasthan; detailed parental occupations not well documented in reviewed English-language sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IIT Bombay, Bhavish Aggarwal cofounder, India smartphone/ride-hail wave, CTO technical ownership
evidence_summary: Bhati's ≤26 milestone is co-founding Ola as technical cofounder at ~23 with IIT Bombay peer Bhavish Aggarwal. Elite Indian engineering pipeline, complementary cofounder team, and structural mobile-internet ride-hail wave are the clearest advantages; family capital/domain transfer is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born ~1987 in Jodhpur, Rajasthan; IIT Bombay B.Tech mechanical engineering and M.Tech path before founding Ola.
current_position: Co-founder of Ola (stepped back from day-to-day after ~2019); later co-founded Amnic; lower public profile than Bhavish Aggarwal.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Ola Cabs / ANI Technologies with Bhavish Aggarwal as technical cofounder.
Ola launched real-time mobile app booking, shifting from call-center aggregation.
Ola acquired rival TaxiForSure for ~₹1,237 crore amid SoftBank-era scale-up.
Ended primary operating role at Ola after roughly a decade as cofounder/CTO.
Co-founded Amnic after leaving full-time Ola operations.

name: Naveen Tewari
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable founder milestone by age 26 (2003). Co-founded mKhoj (later InMobi) in 2007 at age 29–30 after IIT Kanpur and a Harvard Business School MBA; unicorn status and SoftBank $200M round came in 2011 at age ~33–34.
family_context_summary: Born 14 December 1977 in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, India.
evidence_summary: InMobi/mKhoj founding in 2007 occurred at age ~29–30 following Harvard MBA; India's first ad-tech unicorn story is post-26. No dated material personal milestone by age 26 found in reviewed sources.

name: Tanay Kothari
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Wispr (later Wispr Flow) around 2021 at age ~23 after prior teen products (including Convert.cc with millions of users) and selling FeatherX, an e-commerce personalization startup built around Stanford graduation; Forbes 30 Under 30 (Consumer Technology) in Dec 2022 at age 24.
early_history_summary: India-born coder who taught himself programming around age nine, shipped dozens of apps as a teen (music downloader Convert.cc reportedly hit multi-million users before a Google cease-and-desist), earned Microsoft certifications young, studied CS/AI at Stanford, sold FeatherX, then co-founded voice-interface company Wispr Flow.
family_context_summary: Born and educated in India (Delhi-area childhood stories common in interviews); family occupations not strongly documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen shipping reps, Stanford CS/AI, early product virality, generative voice AI wave
evidence_summary: Kothari had extensive product reps before 20 and co-founded Wispr Flow at ~23 after an earlier acquisition. Stanford pipeline and extreme early online shipping practice are documented; family capital/domain advantages are not. Wispr later scaled into a high-valuation voice AI company post-26.
starting_point: Born 4 March 1998 in India; self-taught coding from about age nine in a Delhi-area upbringing before Stanford CS/AI.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Wispr Flow (voice-first AI interface), widely reported multi-hundred-million valuation and large funding rounds as of 2025–2026.

trajectory.event: Built Convert.cc music product that reportedly reached millions of users before a Google cease-and-desist.
Around Stanford CS/AI studies, built and sold FeatherX e-commerce personalization startup (acquired by Cerebra).
Co-founded Wispr (later Wispr Flow) to build a voice interface / neural-interface product.
Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Consumer Technology.
Pivoted Wispr from hardware-leaning silent-speech concept toward Flow desktop voice software product-market fit.
Raised large growth rounds; company widely covered as a high-valuation voice AI startup.

name: Karan Goel
milestone_by_age_26: No clear material independently verifiable breakout by age 26 (~2018). Landmark S4 state-space sequence model paper (arXiv Nov 2021; ICLR 2022) and Cartesia founding (2023) occurred around ages ~29–31 after IIT Delhi EE, CMU ML master's (2018, Siebel Scholar), and Stanford PhD. CMU master's/Siebel award at ~26 is strong education, not a product or research breakout of the required bar.
family_context_summary: Grew up in New Delhi around a family scientific equipment manufacturing business reported as ~125 years old.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family scientific equipment manufacturing business provided entrepreneurship and technical-industry proximity.
evidence_summary: Cartesia and the S4 research line that underpins it are post-26 achievements. Family industrial background and elite CS pipeline are notable but do not substitute for a dated ≤26 material milestone under the rubric.

name: Aditya Grover
category: ML researcher / diffusion LLM cofounder (Inception Labs)
milestone_by_age_26: Published node2vec (KDD 2016 with Jure Leskovec), a foundational network representation-learning paper with 16k+ citations, at about age 22 while a Stanford PhD student shortly after IIT Delhi undergrad (2015).
early_history_summary: IIT Delhi CSE bachelor's (2011–2015), then Stanford CS PhD (2015–2020) advised in the Leskovec/AI ecosystem. node2vec became a default graph embedding method; later work spanned generative models, decision-making under limited supervision, climate foundation models (ClimaX), UCLA faculty, and co-founding Inception Labs for diffusion LLMs.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in India; detailed parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IIT Delhi, Stanford SNAP/Leskovec lab, node2vec open-source, graph ML wave
evidence_summary: Grover's age-22 node2vec paper is a clear, dated, multi-source research milestone with enduring impact. Elite IIT→Stanford pipeline and collaboration with Jure Leskovec are the strongest early advantages; family background is not documented. Later UCLA faculty, Forbes 30 Under 30 (age ~29), and Inception Labs cofounding extend the trajectory after 26.
starting_point: Born ~1994 and raised in India; IIT Delhi CSE bachelor's (2015) before Stanford PhD.
current_position: Assistant professor of computer science at UCLA (MINT group); co-founder and CTO of Inception Labs (diffusion/parallel LLMs); Forbes 30 Under 30 Science (2024) and MIT TR Innovators Under 35 (2025).

trajectory.event: Graduated IIT Delhi CSE and began Stanford Computer Science PhD.
Published node2vec (KDD 2016), a foundational graph representation-learning method.
Completed Stanford PhD; thesis later recognized with ACM SIGKDD Doctoral Dissertation Award.
Joined UCLA CS faculty as assistant professor after Berkeley postdoc.
Co-developed ClimaX climate/weather foundation model line; named Forbes 30 Under 30 Science.
Co-founded Inception Labs as CTO, building diffusion-based parallel LLMs.
Received IJCAI Computers and Thought Award and MIT TR Innovators Under 35 recognition.
